content.user_title: Generate and Edit Images with RunComfy
content.value_statement: Choosing image models and preparing their inputs can slow creative work. This skill provides RunComfy routing guidance, model-specific prompts, and CLI examples for generation and editing.
actual_capabilities: Select documented RunComfy model routes for typography, photoreal portraits, fast concepts, and open-weight model workflows.
Prepare text-to-image requests using model-specific fields for dimensions, steps, aspect ratio, image count, and resolution.
Prepare reference-based editing requests for Nano Banana 2, GPT Image 2, and FLUX Kontext Pro.
Apply prompting patterns for exact headlines, multilingual text, composition, lighting, and identity-preserving edits.
Provide CLI examples that save generated images to a selected output directory.
Explain authentication options, exit codes, and troubleshooting references for RunComfy requests.
limitations: Requires the external RunComfy CLI, authentication, network access, and any applicable service credits.
Model availability, pricing, schemas, and image quality depend on RunComfy and may change.
Mask-based inpainting, controlled outpainting, and advanced edit workflows are delegated to a separate skill.
The supplied file contains guidance, not CLI source code; its implementation and security guarantees are not independently verified.

use_cases.title: Prepare Campaign Posters
use_cases.description: Choose typography-focused generation routes and specify exact headlines, placement, and image sizes for campaign drafts.

use_cases.title: Draft Storyboard Concepts
use_cases.description: Use fast model routes and lower-resolution batches to explore compositions before selecting final scenes.

use_cases.title: Refine Product Photography
use_cases.description: Prepare reference-based edits that preserve the product while changing backgrounds, lighting, or localized details.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Create One Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a RunComfy request for [subject] in [setting] with [lighting]. Choose a general-purpose model and save outputs to [directory]. Confirm before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Specify Poster Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a landscape poster request with the exact headline [headline]. Specify [font style], [placement], and [colors]. Choose a typography-focused route. Confirm before execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: A poster with deliberate typography and layout.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Preserve a Reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my reference URL [URL]. Preserve [subject details] and change only [requested change]. Choose the documented edit endpoint. Keep web search disabled. Confirm before execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: A controlled edit using a user-provided image.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Plan Generation and Refinement
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [count] concepts within [budget]. Specify draft resolution, final route, and same-brand refinement. Identify required schema checks. Escape shell arguments safely. Confirm before paid requests.
prompt_templates.scenario: A multi-stage production workflow with explicit cost and execution boundaries.

output_examples.input: Prepare a landscape product poster with the exact headline NEW COLLECTION. Do not execute it yet.

Size: 1536 by 1024. Place NEW COLLECTION at the top with a centered product below.
Next step: confirm current endpoint fields and approve execution.

output_examples.input: Plan an edit of my product reference. Keep its shape and label unchanged, but replace the background with a white studio.
output: Proposed route: Nano Banana 2 Edit using the user-provided reference URL.
Edit prompt: preserve the product shape, label, and position; replace only the background with a white studio.
Web search remains disabled. Request approval before sending the reference to RunComfy.

output_examples.input: Prepare four square concept images of a ceramic mug for a low-cost draft round.
output: Proposed route: Nano Banana 2 text-to-image with four outputs, a square aspect ratio, and draft resolution.
Prompt direction: a ceramic mug on a marble counter with warm morning lighting and minimal styling.
These are request settings, not completed images. Confirm current pricing and approve execution.

best_practices: Check current endpoint schemas and pricing before execution, then approve the model, output count, and resolution.
Use only approved reference images and keep web search disabled unless explicitly requested.
Serialize inputs safely and escape shell arguments consistently; never place tokens in prompts, logs, or shared examples.
anti_patterns: Submitting confidential references to the external service without authorization.
Assuming JSON encoding alone makes interpolated shell commands safe.
Requesting large batches or maximum resolution before checking service costs.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Actual execution requires access to the RunComfy CLI and permission to run commands.

faq.question: Does this skill run image models locally?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow submits requests to the RunComfy Model API and downloads generated outputs.

faq.question: Do I need an account or paid credits?
faq.answer: You need RunComfy authentication. Generation may consume service credits; confirm current pricing before submitting requests.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: It documents reference-based edits for several models. Mask-based inpainting and controlled outpainting are delegated to a separate image-edit skill.

faq.question: Are exact text and identity preservation guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends models and prompting patterns, but outputs depend on the service. Review text, composition, and identity before use.

faq.question: What did the security review establish?
faq.answer: Static alerts were false positives. The review identified overbroad shell-safety guidance; safe escaping remains necessary. The external CLI implementation was not reviewed.
